rics.description: Average Earnings YY, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, year-over-year change — the headline wage-inflation gauge from the BLS establishment survey, released with NFP. Captures pay growth across all private nonfarm employees.
rics.how_to_use: Markets watch this for Fed implications: AHE growth above ~4% is incompatible with 2% inflation absent a productivity miracle. Less reliable than ECI (aUSEMPCI/A) at turning points because it's sensitive to compositional shifts (when low-wage hospitality jobs are cut, the average mechanically rises).

rics.description: Average earnings- Actual, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings month-over-month change — monthly wage-growth pulse from BLS establishment survey, released with NFP.
rics.how_to_use: Monthly wage-momentum read. >0.4% MoM hot (sustained ~5% YoY pace), <0.2% cool (sustained ~2.5% YoY). Highly volatile month-to-month due to compositional shifts and timing — smooth with 3-month moving average for cleaner signal.

rics.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, durable goods
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, durable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Manufacturing wages, durables. Less sensitive to services wage spirals.

rics.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, total manufacturing — narrower than headline AHE. Captures shop-floor manufacturing wage levels (excludes supervisory/administrative).
rics.how_to_use: Track for industrial-sector wage pressure separately from services. Manufacturing wages matter for unit labor costs and for international competitiveness. Watch alongside non-manufacturing services wages (aUSEARNHS/A) for broad wage pressure picture.

rics.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, nondurable goods
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, nondurable manufacturing — wages at food, chemicals, paper, plastics, textiles plants. Less cyclical than durables wages.
rics.how_to_use: Less cyclical than durables (aUSWRIMDB/A) because nondurable demand (food, consumer staples) is more stable. Use for tracking wage pressure in stable-demand manufacturing. Diverges from durables in recessions — durables wage growth slows faster.

rics.description: Average hourly earnings, construction
rics.meaning: AHE all employees, construction.
rics.how_to_use: Construction wages — key for housing affordability and infrastructure cost models.

rics.description: Average hourly earnings, manufacturing, durable goods
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings, manufacturing, durable goods, all employees — wages in autos, machinery, electronics, metals, transportation equipment. Broader (all-employees) than production-only series.
rics.how_to_use: Most cyclical wage measure — durable manufacturing has the most volatile demand. Watch as a leading wage indicator: durables wages turn before headline. Useful proxy for skilled-trades wage pressure.

rics.description: Average producion workers, durable goods
rics.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, durable goods manufacturing — hours-per-worker measure. Pro-cyclical: rises in booms (overtime), falls in slowdowns (hours cuts before layoffs).
rics.how_to_use: Leading labor-market indicator: hours cuts come before layoffs. Sustained drop below 40 hours/week historically signals manufacturing recession. Combined with manufacturing employment, gives total labor input for productivity calculations.

rics.description: Average producion workers, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, total manufacturing — combined durable + nondurable. Pro-cyclical: rises in booms, falls in slowdowns.
rics.how_to_use: Manufacturing-hours cuts precede manufacturing-employment cuts by 1-3 months. Watch for sub-40-hour readings as recession-leading indicators. Combined with aUSWKIMDA (durables) for cyclical sub-segment read.

rics.description: Average producion workers, nondurable goods
rics.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, nondurable manufacturing — hours in food, chemicals, paper, plastics, textiles. Less cyclical than durables.
rics.how_to_use: More stable than durable-goods hours. Useful as a baseline for stripping out cyclical demand effects. Sustained drops here (rare) would signal broad-based manufacturing-recession risk.

rics.description: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm , durable goods
rics.meaning: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm durable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Take-home pay proxy. Hours × hourly wage.

rics.description: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm manufacturing — hours × hourly wage for manufacturing workers. Take-home pay proxy for industrial-sector labor.
rics.how_to_use: Combines wage and hours signals. Watch alongside services weekly earnings (aUSWEIPB/A) for pay-growth-by-sector picture. Manufacturing weekly wages have grown slower than services since 2010 — structural shift.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, AVG HOURLY REAL EARNINGS OF ALL EMPLOYEES - TOTAL PRIVATE
rics.meaning: Real average hourly earnings, all employees, total private.
rics.how_to_use: Inflation-adjusted wages. Stagnant for years; 2022-23 had negative real wage growth.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm goods producing industries
rics.meaning: AHE, nonfarm goods-producing industries.
rics.how_to_use: Goods-producing wage gauge. Cycles with manufacturing/construction.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
rics.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings of all private nonfarm employees — level (not change). The headline wage series released alongside NFP each month from the BLS establishment survey. Around $35/hour in recent prints.
rics.how_to_use: The level itself is rarely traded; markets focus on the YoY change (aUSAHVEA) as a wage-inflation gauge. Use the level for compositional adjustments and to track real wages (deflate by CPI). Production and nonsupervisory wages (separate series) are a cleaner signal of low-wage worker bargaining power.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm payrolls, all employees, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Average hourly earnings, nonfarm manufacturing, all employees — broader (all-employees) than production-only series. Includes supervisory + admin.
rics.how_to_use: More inclusive than production-only AHE. Tracks total compensation pressure in manufacturing. Use for unit-labor-cost calculations alongside productivity (aUSPHOPBUS/A).

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm service-producing industries
rics.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, services-providing nonfarm — wages in healthcare, leisure, professional services, retail, finance, education. ~85% of the workforce.
rics.how_to_use: Drives core services CPI inflation — services-sector wage growth above ~4% sustains 2-3% core services inflation. The Fed's most-cited wage-pressure measure. Decompose by sub-sector: leisure/hospitality wages spiked 2021-22 then normalized; healthcare wages still rising structurally.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm, all private employees
rics.meaning: AHE all private employees — alternate series.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check with aUSEARNH/A.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm, all private employees, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: AHE all private employees YoY change.
rics.how_to_use: Wage inflation. >4% YoY too hot for 2% inflation; <3% suggests easing.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, nonfarm, manufacturing (all employees) — same conceptual measure as aUSWAGMANB/A. Cross-check series.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSWAGMANA. Use whichever has fresher data. The 'all-employees' framing has been the BLS standard since 2006 reform.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Real average, total private
rics.meaning: Real AHE, total private.
rics.how_to_use: Inflation-adjusted; the wage-gain that actually buys things.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
rics.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, total private nonfarm — hourly wage × hours worked per week. Pre-tax weekly take-home gauge.
rics.how_to_use: More cyclical than hourly wages because hours worked are pro-cyclical (overtime cut in slowdowns, expanded in booms). Better predictor of consumer spending than hourly wage alone. Watch for divergence: when hours fall while hourly wage rises, total income may flatten.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
rics.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, nonfarm payroll, total private — annual aggregate companion to aUSEARN at lower frequency.
rics.how_to_use: Long-time-series wages tracking. Use aUSEARN for monthly tracking. Real version (deflated by CPI, aUSEARNW/CA) is the most analytically useful for household-income trend.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payrolls, all employees, total private
rics.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, nonfarm, all employees (private) — broader than production-only weekly earnings. Includes supervisory + admin staff.
rics.how_to_use: More inclusive than aUSEARN (production-only). Use for total private-sector wage-pressure tracking. Diverges from production weekly earnings when supervisory-vs-production hiring mix shifts.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Real average, total private
rics.meaning: Real average weekly earnings — average weekly earnings deflated by CPI. Best take-home-pay-after-inflation gauge for tracking household real-income trends.
rics.how_to_use: The single best 'how is the typical worker doing' indicator. Negative real wage growth (2021-22) drives consumer-confidence collapses; recovery (2024+) supports spending. Track alongside real disposable personal income (DPI) for full household-cash-flow picture.

rics.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Total Private
rics.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, total private, alternative source — companion series to aUSWEIPB/A.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. Useful for revisions tracking.

rics.description: Earnings, Total Private, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Total private earnings MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Monthly wage momentum.

rics.description: Payroll index, Producion workers, durable goods
rics.meaning: Payroll index, production workers durable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Production-worker payroll proxy.

rics.meaning: Payroll index, production workers nondurable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Nondurables version.

rics.description: Payroll index, production workers, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Payroll index, production workers, manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Total mfg payroll index.

rics.description: Payrolls Benchmark NSA
rics.meaning: Payrolls benchmark NSA — annual benchmark revision.
rics.how_to_use: BLS preliminary payroll benchmark; signals direction of QCEW-based annual revision (typically large in 2024-25).

rics.description: Payrolls Benchmark SA
rics.meaning: Payrolls benchmark, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: SA version. Big negative revisions (e.g., -800k in 2024) reset NFP narrative.

rics.description: Weekly payroll index, durable goods
rics.meaning: Weekly payroll index, durable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Hourly × weekly hours payroll proxy.

rics.description: Weekly payroll index, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Weekly payroll index, manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Total mfg weekly payroll proxy.

rics.meaning: Weekly payroll index, nondurable goods.
rics.how_to_use: Nondurables version.
